chapter: Mutes, influences and the blues singers
title: Dyer Jones's daughter Dolly Jones
summary: Her daughter Dolly, also a trumpeter, was helped by Louis Armstrong and played more modern changes.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: And Dyer and Louie were friends. They knew each other. They -- I guess he must have helped her some time too, in the -- you know, happenings there. But the daughter was very nice, real sweet, and -- but she had -- at that time she told me she was inspired by a lot of trumpet players, and one in particular who had inspired me. He was with -- had been with Don Redman, different bands. Hmmm -- he's working now for the airplane company. He's working out in Jamaica -- Long Island there. Oh, what the heck is his name? You know. Oh boy, what a trumpet player.

Anyway, he had taught her, showed her a lot of things, and helped her, and she was more a modern, I would say, modern gig, because she was playing more changes, running the changes, what we -- you know what we mean by changes, the kind -- the -- uh!
Harmony -- yeah, the chords. Harmony, running the changes renditions. And she could do very, very well and sounded doggone good.
What was the duaghter's name? Do you remember?
Well, she's the lady. But I haven't seen Dolly in so many years. I hope she's well and doing fine, but --
